title: Unlocking Continuous Diffusion Language Models via Discrete Stochastic Localization
claim: Parallel generation need not be synchronized: each element localizes toward a discrete anchor at its own noise level, moving from masked to hard.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; geometric trajectory plot beside a color-coded state table
description: Two panels. The left panel is a 2-D toy geometry plot. Five labeled symbol anchors A–E sit as colored dots around a central origin and are joined to it by dashed lines. Jagged colored trajectories, labeled z1 to z4, wander from the center toward their anchors. Gray, blue, purple and orange mark different tokens, and faint gray noise paths lie in the background. The right panel is a table with columns Token 1 to Token 5. Its rows are State (z1, z5, z2, z3, z4), SNR (0.0, 1.0, 1.4, 9.3, 24.3) and Decoded. The Decoded row has color-matched boxes: B (mask), A (soft), C (soft), D (soft), E (hard). The colors tie the table cells to the trajectories on the left. The eye goes first to the colorful trajectories, then to the table.
caption: Discrete Stochastic Localization (DSL) dynamically "localizes" to sample discrete tokens. (Left) DSL dynamics on a cyclic toy sequence (ABCDE, BCDEA, \ldots); details in Appendix [ref]. (Right) State summary at one snapshot: each token occupies a different SNR regime, transitioning from masked to soft to hard decoding as SNR increases.
abstract: Continuous diffusion is a natural framework for non-autoregressive generation but has generally lagged behind masked discrete diffusion models (MDMs) on discrete sequence generation. We argue that continuous diffusion can effectively model discrete sequences through the joint design of noise parameterization and token representation geometry. We introduce \emph{Discrete Stochastic Localization} (DSL), a continuous-state framework that combines a stochastic localization channel with unit-sphere token embeddings, resulting in a Bayes-optimal denoiser that depends only on the noisy state, without additional timestep conditioning. A single trained denoising network then supports multiple sampling methods, from continuous denoising to masked diffusion, random-order autoregressive generation and hybrid continuous-then-discrete generation. Parallel generation in this continuous-state framework, therefore, need not imply synchronized denoising: some tokens can establish context earlier while others remain open to refinement. Fine-tuning a pretrained MDLM checkpoint with DSL substantially improves generation quality, as measured by MAUVE, on OpenWebText across all step budgets from $T{=}128$ to $T{=}1024$. The same checkpoint supports random-order autoregressive sampling, and a hybrid continuous-then-discrete sampler using as few as $T=48$ total steps, without distillation or further training.
